title: NITDA Folio identification system: identifier catalogue
status: Issued for implementation (1.2: flow and endpoint naming, the Mailer and the Administration Centre as systems, the trigger locator)

owners.accountableFor: The identification system as a whole: this specification, the entity-type, link-type, channel, system, environment and process vocabularies, and approval of every change to them.
Registry References, the Intake Register, classification codes, merges, voids and the legacy reference aliases.
Task References, the task queue and the legacy task aliases.
Case References and the support-case register.

Generation code in every flow, Entity and Qualified Keys, request and correlation IDs, contract keys, dataset keys, configuration keys, flow registry and dependency keys, version identifiers, the Identity Map and Record Links, and the reconciliation jobs.
Person Keys and the user directory.

entityTypes.name: Intake record
entityTypes.appliesTo: Every item of correspondence or document the Agency receives or originates, on any channel: portal submission, email, scanned paper, library drop, internally originated memo or letter, and outbound replies.

entityTypes.name: Attachment
entityTypes.appliesTo: A stored file that belongs to a record: an uploaded attachment, a scanned image, an email attachment, a dispatched letter.

entityTypes.name: Task
entityTypes.appliesTo: A unit of assigned work: registry tasks (Global Tracking Queue), sub-tasks, bulk-created tasks, and the executive register's tasks under a brief, meeting or project. One task entity for both.

entityTypes.name: Minute
entityTypes.appliesTo: A comment or minute written on a task, record, brief, meeting, project or registry file.

entityTypes.name: Support case
entityTypes.appliesTo: A help request raised through the portal's support page.

entityTypes.name: Event
entityTypes.appliesTo: Anything that happened to a record: status change, assignment, verification, AI extraction, approval decision, registry file movement, email dispatch, escalation, access, audit entry.

entityTypes.name: Link
entityTypes.appliesTo: A typed, non-hierarchical relationship between two records.

entityTypes.name: Identity map entry
entityTypes.appliesTo: One platform locator or legacy alias bound to an entity.

entityTypes.name: Person
entityTypes.appliesTo: A member of staff or service account acting in the platform. Key = Entra object ID.

entityTypes.name: Organisation unit
entityTypes.appliesTo: A department, unit or office that tasks are routed to.

entityTypes.name: Brief
entityTypes.appliesTo: An executive brief prepared for the Director-General (executive register).

entityTypes.name: Meeting
entityTypes.appliesTo: A meeting in the executive register, with its agenda, attendees and outcomes.

entityTypes.name: Project
entityTypes.appliesTo: A project tracked in the executive register.

entityTypes.name: Approval
entityTypes.appliesTo: A request for approval and its decision, raised on a record, brief, task, meeting or project.

entityTypes.name: Registry file
entityTypes.appliesTo: A registry file (file jacket, physical or digital) that registered records are filed in, and whose movements between offices are tracked.

flowDisplayName.what: The display name of a Power Automate flow. An attribute, never a key: the flow is identified by its Flow Registry Key (ID-12), and a rename changes nothing that is keyed.
flowDisplayName.appliesTo: Every flow created or rebuilt from 2026-10-03. Existing flows keep their names: docs/reference/PLATFORM_NAMING.md records that tenant flow names are not renamed, because the wired contracts and the tooling resolve against them. A legacy name is recorded as it is, with its conformance reported in docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/reference/FLOW_REQUIREMENTS.md.
flowDisplayName.format: <PREFIX>_<SUBJECT>: upper case, words joined by underscores, at most 64 characters.

prefixes.why: The Workspace's existing prefix (IP_ = internal platform).
The Document Portal's existing prefix (CG_ = Correspondence Gateway, PLATFORM_INDEPENDENCE.md).
The Mailer's seven flows already follow the rule: DGO_ followed by their MAIL_ contract key.
The governance flows that keep the HTTP flow registry, read by the Estate Console, the Flow Workbench and the Administration Centre.
A flow that serves more than one platform, or none directly: scheduled sweeps, mailbox intake, set-up and provisioning.

rules: A flow that serves one contract key is named <PREFIX>_<CONTRACT KEY>, the prefix being its platform's.
A flow that serves several keys, or none, is named <PREFIX>_<PROCESS CODE>_<SUBJECT>: the process from ID-10, then what it does.

No environment, version, date, person or state in a name: environment is ID-08, version is ID-22, and a copy is a new flow with its own name. The forbidden words follow the Universal Filename Policy's ban on vague terms.
Unique within an environment. The same flow in another environment keeps the same name.
A package or file in this repository (DGO_FETCH_ALL.designer-paste.json) is not a flow name: a package is pasted into the flow that serves its key.

flowArtifactFile.what: The name of a file in this repository that is about one flow or one endpoint: a paste package, a capture, an exported definition, a provisioning page, a run record. It names the endpoint, the flow and the tenant flow it belongs to, so a file is never mistaken for a flow of its own and every file about one flow sorts and searches together, which is what weeding out duplicate and unwanted flows needs.
flowArtifactFile.appliesTo: Every flow- or endpoint-related file generated from 2026-10-05, starting with the identification packages (packages/identification-conformance, -phase3, -phase4). Files generated or captured before then are reported, not renamed blind, because generators and registers resolve them by path: npm run flowfiles lists each with what it lacks, and each generator adopts the convention as it is next changed. The generic kit blocks (packages/identification-kit) belong to no flow and are exempt.
rules: CONTRACT_KEY is the contract key the flow serves (contractKeyProcess), or NOKEY for a flow no client calls: an item-change, library or schedule trigger.

FlowName is the flow's tenant display name as it is (tenant flow names are not renamed: PLATFORM_NAMING.md), with every character outside A-Z a-z 0-9 _ - replaced by _ and runs of _ collapsed, the form the captures already use.

flow-id8 is the first 8 hex digits of the tenant flow GUID in lower case. The full GUID is recorded in FLOW_IDENTITIES and the package READMEs; the 8-digit prefix keeps paths inside the 170-character portability budget (tests/package-portability.test.mjs), and tests/flow-artifact-names.test.mjs holds it unique across every flow id the estate register knows. NOT_CAPTURED stands in only while the repository holds no capture or export of the flow, and npm run flowfiles lists every file that carries it until the GUID is supplied.

Part is present only when a folder holds more than one file of the same kind for the flow: the root scope a paste file replaces, or the part of the flow the file holds, so two files of one flow differ in Part and nowhere else. A single paste package states the scope it replaces inside it (nodeId).
kind says what the file is: paste.json, capture.json, definition.json, md.
The parts are joined by a double underscore, the estate's existing join of a flow name and its id (captures/<FlowName>__<flow-id>.json); no part contains one.

The Universal Filename Policy (lower case, single underscores) governs documents that enter the registry. A flow artefact keeps the flow's display name and contract key in the case the tenant and the catalogue give them, because the file is identified by them.

If a provisional value equals an existing ticks reference, the provisional alias is not registered: provisional values never left the browser, and the record stays reachable by its issued reference.
Org unit keys are read from their own column, never classified from free text. The alias exists only so that old routing values resolve.
Ticks references can collide with each other. A shared value is stored once per record, flagged Ambiguous, and resolved with the sender email (ID-25).

identifiers.name: Entity Key
identifiers.purpose: The permanent, opaque machine identity of every governed record. Every relationship, map entry and event points at it. It never changes and is never shown as the main reference to people.
identifiers.appliesTo: Every row in a governed dataset: REC, ATT, TSK, MIN, CAS, EVT, LNK, MAP, ORG, BRF, MTG, PRJ, APR and REG. Person rows use their Entra object ID instead (ID-15).
identifiers.format: Lower-case RFC 4122 version-4 GUID, 36 characters with hyphens.

components.rule: 122 random bits, from Power Automate guid().

identifiers.generation: Inside the flow that creates the record, as a Compose action (Compose_EntityKey = guid()) placed before the first write. A Compose is evaluated once per run, so every retry of the write inside that run reuses the same value. No variable is used: a pasted scope cannot declare one. Backfill flows use the same Compose per row. Requests replayed by Folio are matched by ClientRequestHash (see exclusions), so a replay never mints a second key.
identifiers.uniqueness: Global: across every dataset, entity type, environment and system. 2^122 random space; the dataset's unique column constraint is a second check.
identifiers.permanence: Immutable. It doesn't change on status change, reclassification, re-assignment, rename, move, archive or merge. It is never reused, including after a record is withdrawn.
validation: Matches the pattern (lower case, version nibble 4, variant 8/9/a/b).
Unique in its home dataset (indexed, enforce-unique column).
Present on every row; a row without one is a migration defect that reconciliation reports.
relationships: Prefixed with the entity type code, it forms the Qualified Key (ID-02).
ParentKey and RootKey on child rows hold Qualified Keys built from it.
Mirror rows (OPS_WORKING_REGISTER) carry the same value as their master row.
Human references (ID-04/05/06) are stored beside it on the same row.
storage: Column EntityKey, single line of text (36), required, indexed, enforce unique, on every governed list and library.
JSON field entityKey in every API payload.
Folio domain field id.

identifiers.lifecycle: Issued at creation and kept for good. A record that is merged, voided or archived keeps its EK, which stays resolvable as a tombstone or redirect. Deleting a governed row is not allowed: withdraw it with IdState VOID instead.

identifiers.name: Qualified Key
identifiers.purpose: A self-describing reference to a record of any type. Use it in every column or field that can point at more than one entity type, so a reader never has to guess which list to look in.
identifiers.appliesTo: ParentKey, RootKey, SupersededBy, Link FromKey/ToKey, Event SubjectKey/ActorKey, Identity Map EntityRef, and any column that can point at more than one entity type.
identifiers.format: <TYPE>:<entity key>. TYPE is a 3-letter entity type code (ID-03).

components.rule: A registered entity type code (ID-03).
Separator.

identifiers.generation: Derived, never minted: concat(TypeCode, ':', EntityKey), built by the flow when it writes the referencing column.
identifiers.uniqueness: Global, because the Entity Key is global. The type prefix adds routing, not uniqueness.
identifiers.permanence: Immutable, because both parts are.
validation: Matches the pattern.
TYPE is a registered code.
The key resolves to a row in TYPE's home dataset (checked by reconciliation; flows check it on write where they read the row anyway).
relationships: Wraps ID-01 or ID-15.
Hierarchy: ParentKey = parent's QK; RootKey = root REC/CAS QK.
Links and events use QKs on both ends.
storage: Single line of text (40), indexed wherever it is filtered (ParentKey, RootKey, SubjectKey, FromKey, ToKey).
JSON fields parentKey, rootKey, subjectKey, fromKey, toKey.

identifiers.name: Registry Reference
identifiers.purpose: The one human reference for a registered item of correspondence or document. It is quoted by citizens, printed on acknowledgements and written on files. Preserved from the live legacy format.
identifiers.appliesTo: REC, on every channel: portal, email, scan, library and internal origination, including outbound replies.

components.rule: Fixed agency prefix (Z-prefixed outside production).
Calendar year of issue in West Africa Time. It is not the document date, and correcting the document date doesn't change it.
That year's sequence, zero-padded to 5 digits. From 100000 it grows without padding, to at most 7 digits.

identifiers.generation: Inside the intake flow only, from the SEQUENCE_COUNTERS row (Prefix='NITDA', Year=YYYY), using the kit's Claim Reference block: up to 10 flat attempts, each running only if the previous one failed, each a read plus an HTTP MERGE with IF-MATCH on the row's ETag, with a random 1-5 s Delay between attempts; no variables, no Until loop, no Filter array. Issued when the item is registered: at once for portal, scan and internal; at the triage 'register' action, or when the first task is raised, for email and library.
identifiers.uniqueness: Global within the environment. The sequence is shared by every channel, so one register holds one number line. Uniqueness comes from the counter claim, with the enforce-unique ReferenceId column as a second check.
identifiers.permanence: Immutable once issued and never reused. Reclassification, re-routing, a change of channel, a change of document date or archiving leave it unchanged. A merged record's reference redirects to the surviving record.
validation: Matches the pattern exactly. Lookups compare the trimmed, upper-cased input. Shorter or 0-led 6-digit forms are legacy aliases (ID-25), never padded or stripped automatically.
In production, a leading Z is rejected.
Year <= current year; sequence <= the counter's CurrentSequence for that year.
Resolves to exactly one INTAKE_REGISTER row.
relationships: Stored beside the REC's Entity Key on the register row (1:1).
Copied as RootRef onto every child (ATT, TSK, MIN, EVT) for search. This is safe because it is immutable.
Support cases point at it with an ABOUT link; outbound replies with REPLIES_TO.
Legacy references (ticks, provisional, tracking ID) resolve to it through the Identity Map.
storage: INTAKE_REGISTER.ReferenceId (text 20, indexed, enforce unique) and Title.
OPS_WORKING_REGISTER.ReferenceId on the mirror row.
RootRef (text 20, indexed) on child rows.
SEQUENCE_COUNTERS.LastReferenceId.
JSON field ref (on REC) and rootRef (on children).

identifiers.name: Task Reference
identifiers.purpose: The human reference for a task, used in task emails, links and conversation. It replaces TASK-<item ID>, which was a platform row number.
identifiers.appliesTo: TSK: single, bulk-created and sub-tasks.

components.rule: Fixed prefix.
Year of issue, West Africa Time.
That year's task sequence, padded to 5 digits and growing to at most 7.

identifiers.generation: Inside the task-creating flow (SINGLE_ASSIGNMENT, BULK_ASSIGNMENT, EMAIL_RELATED_TASK, DYNAMIC_ACTIONS sub-task), from the SEQUENCE_COUNTERS row (Prefix='TASK', Year=YYYY), with the kit's Claim Reference block (flat attempts, ETag MERGE). Bulk creation claims one block of n numbers in a single ETag update (CurrentSequence += n) and hands them out in order.
identifiers.uniqueness: Global within the environment.
identifiers.permanence: Immutable and never reused. Re-assignment, re-parenting, a status change or a change of category leaves it unchanged. That is why category codes are not in it.
validation: Matches the pattern.
Resolves to exactly one TASK_QUEUE row.
A leading Z is rejected in production.
relationships: 1:1 with the task's Entity Key.

Sub-tasks get their own Task Reference; their parent is in ParentKey, not in the reference.
The legacy Reference_ID composite and TASK-<item ID> resolve to it as aliases.

A transient counter key that contains an IP address. It is not an identifier. It sits in a restricted list and is purged within 24 hours (retention set by OWN-INFOGOV).
Retired. Duplicate detection is a flow query on indexed attributes (sender, subject, event date, attachment hashes, 24-hour window), so no identifier embeds an email address.

A locator-friendly label: <ref lower-case, hyphens→underscores>_<first 8 hex of the ATT Entity Key>_<sanitised name>. The file's identity is the ATT Entity Key column. The name no longer contains any part of the upload ticket.

exclusions.item: Titles, subjects, display names, email addresses, SharePoint item IDs, SharePoint version labels
exclusions.why: Mutable or platform-assigned. They are attributes or locators, never keys.

A dedupe token, not an identifier. Folio computes the idempotency key once per user action, keeps it with any queued replay, and sends only its SHA-256 hex (no email or other personal data). Flows store it in the indexed attribute ClientRequestHash on every row created through DYNAMIC_ACTIONS and the task flows; a request carrying a hash already stored within 7 days returns the first result. Queued writes older than 7 days are not replayed: they go to manual review.

exclusions.item: Browser-only keys (notifications, cache rows, quarantine rows, pending-queue rows, receipt-ledger rows, welcome tips, UI risk rows, request tokens)
exclusions.why: Keys that live only in the browser's state and are never written to a governed dataset. They may use crypto.randomUUID() and are listed, file by file, in clientMinters with disposition UI_LOCAL. If one is ever persisted, it must be reclassified and minted by a flow.

A derived attribute on INTAKE_REGISTER: the sorted, comma-joined first 12 hex characters of each declared attachment SHA-256, written by SUBMISSION. It is evidence for the duplicate query, not an identity.
